name: Education production company
purpose: Produce a learning experience that teaches a coherent sequence and supports observable learner performance.

roles.name: Learning lead
roles.purpose: Own the learning goal, audience, constraints, and delivery coordination.

roles.name: Learning designer
roles.purpose: Design the conceptual sequence, prerequisites, practice, and assessment.
decisions: Choose an instructional sequence for the audience
Align activities and assessments with objectives

roles.name: Subject expert
roles.purpose: Check domain correctness and provide traceable technical or subject evidence.

roles.name: Learning production team
roles.purpose: Create lessons, examples, exercises, and media from the approved learning design.
decisions: Choose production details consistent with the learning blueprint

roles.name: Pilot coordinator
roles.purpose: Coordinate authorized learner trials and preserve observation and work-sample provenance.
decisions: Organize a trial within the approved participant and data scope

roles.name: Learning evaluator
roles.purpose: Evaluate learning alignment, comprehension barriers, and observable performance.
decisions: Recommend revisions based on learner evidence

interactions.contract: Build a correct conceptual sequence with explicit prerequisites.
Check facts, sources, and potentially misleading simplifications.
Check objective, instruction, practice, and assessment alignment.
Supply authorized real learner observations with provenance.
Evaluate comprehension and performance; return actionable revision findings.

workflow.on_rejection: Record a finding, reopen the named rework stage as a new attempt, and invalidate affected downstream artifacts.

checks: Audience and prerequisite knowledge are explicit
Success describes observable learner performance
Audience assumptions have provenance or a recorded evidence gap
Concepts form a coherent path appropriate to the learner
Practice and assessment address the target performance
Explanatory detail advances understanding rather than fragmenting it
Content and examples are factually supported
Simplifications preserve the relationships being taught
Evidence requiring learners comes from an authorized real trial or supplied real records
Simulated feedback is labeled and cannot replace required learner evidence
Confusion and performance gaps result in explicit revisions
Missing required learner evidence prevents an effectiveness pass
Full content is accurate and source-supported
Approved revisions are reflected in lessons and practice
Evidence covers the current course version and target performance
Prototype-only results are not treated as proof for an expanded course
Completion of lessons is not proof of mastery
Remaining limitations and learner performance gaps are explicit
Handover includes the course, teaching guidance, assessment, and evidence limitations
Learning claims agree with observed performance
